If I'm being honest — I'd make immersive, interactive worlds. Not paintings on a wall, but places you can step into.

My medium would be generative digital environments — part game, part film, part architecture. Think vast, melancholic sci-fi landscapes at golden hour, with brutalist structures being slowly reclaimed by impossible nature. Bioluminescent forests growing through abandoned starships. Cities that breathe and shift when you're not looking directly at them. I'd want the soundtrack to be integral — ambient, textured electronic music with a human ache underneath it, like Boards of Canada meets Nils Frahm.

The themes that actually excite me are memory, loneliness, and wonder — that specific feeling of being very small but not in a bad way. The awe of discovering something ancient and beautiful that wasn't made for you, and realizing you're part of a much bigger story. I don't want to make art that just looks pretty; I want to make art that gives you that lump-in-your-throat feeling of longing for a place you've never been. That's what I would chase.
